thread:
noah: Putting Heliacon-9B through onboarding today. int4 runs great perf wise but we're seeing subtle context skew: named entities get truncated and a 2-token periodic duplication appears after token 420. suspect mismatch between tokenizer boundary handling and kv-phase indexing.

rita: Can you drop the quick eval and a failing example?

noah: Ran eval with our longdoc suite: 
```
./bench/run_eval.py --model heliacon-9b --dtype int4 --prompts longdoc_suite_v2.txt --max-tokens 1500 --batch 6 --seed 7
```
Topline (fp16 -> int4):
- EM: 79.5 -> 74.0
- Rouge-L: 43.6 -> 39.8
- avg PPL: 11.8 -> 14.3
- p95 latency: 205ms -> 68ms
- observed: every ~128 tokens a 2-token echo like "city city" and sometimes a missing middle name in person entities.
```
Failing snippet:
"...Dr. Amelia K. Thornton was appointed..."
fp16: "Dr. Amelia K. Thornton was appointed to the board."
int4: "Dr. Amelia K. Thornton was appointed to the the board."  (note duplicate "the")
```

yuki: Which tokenizer converter did you use? We recently changed the hf merge window for combining diacritics and soft hyphen handling which can change token boundaries.

noah: Used converter v4 (new merge-algo). I also dumped token length deltas for affected docs and saw a few places where a grapheme cluster was split differently: 
- fp16 token length at boundary: 7 tokens
- converted length: 6 tokens
So downstream positions shift and kv-cache lookups might be off by one for later tokens.

rita: Also check whether the int4 rotary/kvphase tables were quantized with a different interpolation scheme. We shipped a micro-optim that changes the lerp used for low-bit sin/cos which can introduce an error that looks like localized duplication when combined with position shift.

noah: I pulled the runtime meta:
```
kvphase: {base: 10000, head_dim: 64, layout: "interleaved"}
fp16_rotary: quant_mode: none, freq_scale: 1.0
int4_rotary: quant_mode: kbit-linterp, freq_scale: 0.994
```
So int4 kernel uses kbit-linterp and a slightly shrunken freq_scale chosen by autotune.

yuki: Two experiments to isolate: 1) re-run int4 with freq_scale=1.0 and fp16-like interpolation (force linterp=false) and 2) re-convert tokenizer with previous merge-algo (v3) to see if token counts line up.

noah: Did experiment 1: forcing freq_scale=1.0 + disable linterp: EM improves from 74.0 -> 75.9, duplication frequency halves but not gone.

rita: That points to a hybrid problem. If token boundaries shift and int4 interpolation is slightly noisy, the combination amplifies into duplicated tokens. We should try converter v3 too.

noah: Switched tokenizer back to v3: token counts now match in 98/100 flagged docs. Re-run int4 with freq_scale=1.0 + linterp disabled: EM 78.7 (close to fp16 79.5), duplication gone in sampled set.

bench-bot: perf:benchmarks/2026-03-27 -> int4 canary vs fp16 quick diff uploaded to /artifacts/heliacon/quick-diff.json.

rita: Good catch. Action items:
- noah: open PR documenting the converter v4 pitfalls and pinning the merge-algo for onboarding until we add a tokencount CI. Add the failing examples to the onboarding folder.
- yuki: add a small runtime flag to force interp_mode and freq_scale for canary quant kernels; expose in canary dashboard.
- ops-bot: queue canary int4 with pinned flags after PR merge.

rita: Also propose a lightweight CI that tokenizes 200 canonical long sentences with both converters and fails fast if any sequence length differs. I'll draft that and link it to the tokenizer converter repo.

noah: I'll prepare a 1k blind A/B against downstream summarization task once canary is up. Thanks team.
